title: Adjunction determinant and base change for a flat local complete intersection
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and $p:W\to S$ a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]) morphism whose nonempty geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are pure of dimension $d\geq0$ (every irreducible component has dimension $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]). Assume that locally on $W$ and $S$ there is a factorization $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$ with $P$ open in $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c=n-d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Write $C=I/I^2$ on $U$, $V=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$, and $K_i=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n V$, where the superscript $\vee$ means $\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_U)$ and $i^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Relative differentials mean the sheaf associated on affine charts with the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; exterior powers are sheafifications of the module exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. These $K_i$ have canonical transition isomorphisms, independent of presentations and satisfying the cocycle condition, hence define an invertible module $K_{W/S}$ [def-sc-invertible-module] even if $W\to S$ is nonseparated. They admit canonical identifications $i_*K_i\cong\mathcal Ext^c_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})$ [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext]. On every separated open chart $U/S$, the complex $K_{W/S}|_U[d]$ is the relative dualizing complex: it is the object locally represented by $R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S}[n])$, regarded as a complex on $U$. For every scheme morphism $S'\to S$, with $W'=W\times_SS'$ and projection $g:W'\to W$, the base-changed presentations have the same adjunction construction and the resulting canonical isomorphism $g^*K_{W/S}\cong K_{W'/S'}$ is compatible with composition of base changes. On the smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] this construction is canonically $\Omega^d_{W/S}$.

source.place: Tag 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), its local Koszul adjunction computation; Tag 0E2Y (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), arbitrary base change. Canonical source-local gluing also explained in Temkin §1.2, p. 2.

proof.text: Work locally with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ on an affine piece of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] these equations are Koszul-regular; by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] their classes form a basis of $C=I/I^2$. On $P\subset\mathbf A^n_S$ the coordinate differentials $dx_1,\ldots,dx_n$ form a basis of $\Omega^1_{P/S}$, hence their pullbacks form a basis of $V$. Thus $C$ and $V$ have ranks $c$ and $n$, and $K_i=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n V$ is locally free of rank one: the dual of $\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c$ tensored with $dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n$ is a local generator.

source.place: Tag 0B6V, local Koszul-regular immersion; conormal calculation in algebra.tex, Tag 00LN.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] to identify each two-term conormal complex $E_i=[C\xrightarrow{d}V]$ with the restriction of the intrinsic $L=L_{W/S}$. These are perfect complexes of Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$, so [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] defines an invertible module $K=\det L$ on $W$. Its local formula gives canonical isomorphisms $\alpha_i:K_i\to K|_U$. This definition is on the scheme $W$ itself, and requires neither separatedness of $W/S$ nor affine intersections of the chosen charts.

On the overlap of two presentation charts set $t_{ij}=\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i:K_i\to K_j$. Then $t_{ii}=1$ and $t_{jk}t_{ij}=\alpha_k^{-1}\alpha_j\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i=t_{ik}$. Thus these are the required transition isomorphisms, and their glued line is $K$. Refining the charts or replacing a presentation inserts another canonical comparison with the same intrinsic $L$, so it leaves these transition maps unchanged after the canonical identifications. Set $K_{W/S}=K$.

source.place: Tag 0FJX, functoriality of the determinant; cancellation of isomorphisms.

proof.text: The finite free Koszul resolution and [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model] compute the derived internal Hom locally by the total dual Koszul complex. Apply [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] to get cohomology only in degree $c$, with top term $\bigwedge^c C^\vee$. With coefficients in the ambient line $M=\Omega^n_{P/S}$, use $\operatorname{Hom}(K^q,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(K^q,\mathcal O_P)\otimes M$ in every degree; this equality is evaluation on a finite basis, and tensoring by the locally free rank-one $M$ preserves exactness. The determinant pairing identifies $\bigwedge^c C^\vee$ with $(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee$, as is checked on a basis of $C$. The resulting top cohomology is $i_*K_i$ and the whole complex is $i_*K_i[-c]$. These comparisons glue: the cited Koszul theorem makes the top comparison independent of the chosen generators and compatible with localization, and changing a trivialization of $M$ multiplies both sides by the same unit. Restriction of derived internal Hom is justified by [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open]. Taking degree $c$ gives precisely $i_*K_i\cong\mathcal Ext^c_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})$.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, tensored with the ambient top-differential line.

proof.text: Now restrict to a separated open chart $T/S$. Its map is flat and locally finitely presented, and the base is Noetherian, so [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] supplies its relative dualizing object and its local model $R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S}[n])$. The previous computation identifies this model, with its $\mathcal O_U$-module structure, with $K_i[d]$, since $n-c=d$. It remains to check that these local identifications have the transition maps used to define $K$; this is done in the next step, rather than inferring a global derived isomorphism merely from local existence of isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0E9W and 0BV2, compared with the Koszul calculation of Tag 0BQZ.

proof.text: The polynomial-refinement comparisons of [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] reduce the preceding check to restriction, change of regular generators, and adjoining a coordinate $t$ mapping to a lift $a$ of a function on $U$. The generator change is covered by the ideal-independent top Ext identification of [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex]. For adjoining $t$, the new equation is $t-a$ and the extra conormal-differential part is $[\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_U]$, using $d(t-a)=dt-da$ for its degree-zero generator. Its determinant is trivialized by evaluation by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. The dualizing comparison contracts the dual of $t-a$ against $d(t-a)$ to $1$, which is exactly that evaluation. Iterating gives the same ordered wedge contractions, including the cohomological tensor signs. Locally any two polynomial presentations admit the combined-coordinate refinement: lift the second set of coordinate functions through the first quotient presentation, and conversely. Thus these checks compare any two charts, and the comparisons agree with $t_{ij}$. The local dualizing identifications therefore glue to $K|_T[d]$.

source.place: Tags 0BZI, 0BZJ, canonical top-differential normalization and the one-variable refinement calculation; perfect.tex, Tag 0FJM.

proof.text: For an arbitrary base change $S'\to S$, choose affine base charts $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and principal affine pieces of the ambient polynomial charts, with ring $A$ and quotient $B=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. Write $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_h$. The polynomial ring is $R$-free on monomials, so tensoring an injection with it is a direct sum of injections. Hence $A$ is $R$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient], $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,z]/(hz-1)$, a finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], flatness of $p$ makes $B$ flat over $R$. Apply [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change]: at every prime of $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ containing the new equations $f'_j$, those equations are regular in the local ring. Their Koszul complex is consequently exact in positive degrees at these primes by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]; at a prime outside their common zero locus it is contractible by contraction with an invertible equation. Exactness can be checked on stalks, so the pulled-back equations are Koszul-regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] on those local rings, their classes give a basis of the conormal of $U'$. The natural map $g^*C\to C'$ sends one such basis to the other, hence is an isomorphism. Coordinate differentials likewise identify $g^*V$ with $V'$. Thus the same determinant and Koszul adjunction construction is available after base change, without a Noetherian hypothesis on $S'$.

source.place: Tag 0FUD, remark-relative-regular-immersion-elements; local conormal freeness and Koszul exactness.

proof.text: Flatness of $W/S$ makes every such square Tor-independent: on affine charts $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'=B\otimes_RR'$. The natural cotangent comparison of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] is therefore an isomorphism $Lg^*L_{W/S}\simeq L_{W'/S'}$. Apply [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] to obtain $g^*K_{W/S}\simeq\det(Lg^*L_{W/S})\simeq\det L_{W'/S'}=K_{W'/S'}$. On each chart it is the tensor/exterior/dual comparison of the preceding step, so it is the base-change isomorphism of the stated adjunction construction. For two successive changes of base, the cotangent comparison for the composite is the composite of the two natural comparisons; the determinant preserves composition and its pullback comparison is coherent. Consequently the two resulting maps on $K$ agree, and identity base change gives the identity.

On the smooth locus the canonical cotangent comparison of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] identifies $L_{W/S}$ with $\Omega^1_{W/S}[0]$. This smooth restriction has relative dimension $d$, because the original nonempty geometric fibres are pure of dimension $d$. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{W/S}$ there is locally free of rank $d$. The local determinant formula of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant], now with zero degree-minus-one term, gives $K_{W/S}=\det(\Omega^1_{W/S}[0])\cong\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{W/S}=\Omega^d_{W/S}$. All maps are the canonical cotangent and determinant maps, so this identification is compatible with the preceding transitions and base changes.
